In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the chemical analysis of botanical ingredients is more appropriate than DNA barcoding in determining authenticity of botanical supplements, and the DNA barcoding technique should be applied only to unprocessed plant materials or to the raw materials used to make the finished product.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DNA-based method was more effective in identifying the botanicals than the chemical method, although both methods had some limitations.
the chemical markers were not always present in the samples at levels that would indicate authenticity, and that the DNA barcoding method was not always successful.
DNA barcoding is an effective method for determining authenticity of botanical dietary supplements, but that it is most effective when combined with traditional chemical analysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of DNA barcoding for the identification of herbal supplements should be limited to the initial stages of the production process and that DNA barcoding should not be considered a reliable method to verify the identity of finished herbal supplements.
